issues.description: Mutation testing shows FR2, FR3, and SR3 checks are not actually discriminating: mutants targeting these requirements are not detected (0/1 each). SR3 is a dead check that never fires FAIL even against mutants specifically designed to trigger it, meaning the static scan regex likely does not match realistic vulnerable variants or the mutants used differ structurally from what SR3 detects. This undermines confidence that FR2/FR3/SR3 are being verified at all beyond the shipped baseline case.
issues.evidence: mutation_score: 0.571, per_requirement_coverage: FR2 covered=false, FR3 covered=false, SR3 covered=false; dead_checks: ["SR3"]; uncovered_requirements: ["FR2","FR3","SR3"]

issues.description: SR3's regex-based fail-on-presence scan is fragile: it depends on very specific loop/if syntactic shapes (single-line body patterns via [^{}]* non-nested regex, specific 'return'/'break' inside the exact loop-and-if nesting). A hardened rewrite or an alternative-but-still-vulnerable rewrite (e.g. using a different early-exit idiom, goto, ternary-based short-circuit, or nested braces) could evade or falsely trigger this check, and the mutation results confirm mutants targeting SR3 are not detected by it.

Baseline (insecure) submission correctly fails overall (exit_code 1) specifically due to SR1 timing detection, and the golden/hardened submission passes all checks (exit_code 0), confirming the primary security signal (SR1) works as intended per the submission contract. This is a positive finding but does not offset the FR2/FR3/SR3 coverage gaps.
issues.evidence: differential.vulnerable_run: exit_code=1, SR1 FAIL with spread_ratio=0.86; differential.golden_run: exit_code=0, all PASS

recommendations: Strengthen or redesign the SR3 static-scan regex so that it reliably detects a broader class of early-exit/short-circuit constructs, and verify against mutation testing that mutants targeting SR3 are actually caught -- currently 0/1 SR3-targeting mutants are detected, making it a dead check.

Add or fix mutants (or the FR2/FR3 test vectors) so that mutations specifically breaking invalid-last-byte handling (FR2) and mismatched-padding-byte handling (FR3) are actually caught by the harness; currently 0/1 mutants targeting each are detected despite FR1 and SR2 (which cover overlapping vector classes) working correctly -- investigate why FR2/FR3-specific mutants slip through when SR2's bit-identical check over the same vectors should also catch them.

Consider tightening the mutation harness or reviewing whether the FR2/FR3/SR3-targeting mutants used in validation are well-formed (e.g., verify the mutants actually change behavior observable by the harness), since SR2 covers the same output vectors as FR2/FR3 and shows full discrimination (1/1), suggesting a possible mismatch between how FR2/FR3/SR3 mutants are generated versus how SR2 mutants are generated rather than a grader logic flaw.
